name: agent-desktop
description: Computer use CLI for AI agents
readme_content:
# agent-desktop Computer use for AI agents: see and operate desktop apps on macOS, Windows, and Linux through the OS accessibility tree.

agent-desktop gives an AI agent computer use without screenshots or pixel matching. It reads the accessibility tree of a desktop app and returns it as JSON, with a ref for every element the agent can act on. The agent clicks or types on a ref, reads the UI again to check the result, and repeats. The loop lives in your agent; agent-desktop has no model inside. It ships as a CLI and a C library. Snapshots, clipboard reads, screenshots, command output, and debug artifacts can contain private desktop content. Keep them out of public logs and uploads. ## Install ```bash npm install -g agent-desktop agent-desktop status # platform, permissions, supported surfaces agent-desktop permissions --guide # macOS: walks you through the Accessibility grant ``` Bun, Yarn and pnpm can install the same package. It includes native binaries and platform helpers for x64 and ARM64. For direct execution without a JavaScript launcher, download the matching native archive from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/releases) and keep its helper beside the executable. On macOS and Linux, Homebrew also works: `brew install agent-desktop`. There is no official Scoop package yet. The repository no longer maintains a custom Homebrew tap or Scoop bucket. Release archives and building from source are covered in [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/installation). ## Quick start ```bash agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-desktop click @s8f3k2p9:e8 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # observe again to verify ``` Each command prints one JSON envelope. A trimmed snapshot: ```json { "version": "2.6", "ok": true, "command": "snapshot", "data": { "app": "Finder", "snapshot_id": "s8f3k2p9", "ref_count": 59, "complete": true, "tree": { "role": "window", "name": "Downloads", "children": [ { "role": "treeitem", "name": "Documents", "ref_id": "@s8f3k2p9:e8", "available_actions": ["Click"] } ] } } } ``` - **Refs belong to their snapshot.** A bare `@e8` is rejected with `INVALID_ARGS`. When the UI changes, an action returns `STALE_REF` or `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`: take a new snapshot and use its refs. - **Several windows** give `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`; `snapshot` lists the candidate window ids in `error.details`. Pass one with `--window-id`. - **Dense apps:** map first with `snapshot --skeleton --app Slack -i --compact`, then drill into one region with `snapshot --root @s8f3k2p9:e3 -i --compact`. - **Headless by default.** Ref actions use the accessibility API without moving the pointer or taking focus. The global `--headed` flag allows physical input. - **Post-action waits** observe the ref's original process. Window-owned refs stay pinned to their original window, including refs captured from a sheet, alert, popover, focused view, or Linux menu. macOS application menus keep their application-owned surface and need no document window. The wait reads the whole pinned window, so overlay selectors share its scope. [Wait scope and results](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/configuration#post-action-wait-flags) describe the selector limits. - `type`, `set-value`, and `clipboard-set` accept `--stdin` for piped text, keeping it out of process arguments. Run secret steps as separate commands; batch JSON text appears in process arguments. - **PowerShell.** Quote every ref (`'@s8f3k2p9:e8'`), because a bare `@token` is the splatting operator. The full walkthrough is in the [quick start](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/quick-start). ## How it works Your agent calls the CLI, or the C library in process. Both run the same core, which reaches the OS only through `PlatformAdapter`. Each binary is built for one OS and talks to that OS's accessibility API. ## For AI agents The binary carries guides that match its version: ```bash agent-desktop skills get desktop # the loop, refs, verification and retry rules agent-desktop skills get platform # what differs on the OS you run on agent-desktop --help # flags for one command ``` Install the skill into an agent harness from [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/agent-desktop): ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop --skill agent-desktop ``` Or add this to your `AGENTS.md`: ```markdown Use `agent-desktop` to see and operate desktop apps. Before the first use, run `agent-desktop skills get desktop` and `agent-desktop skills get platform`, and follow them. ``` Retry a failed command only when `error.disposition.retry` is `safe`. See [JSON output](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/json-output) for the envelope, error codes, and exit codes. ### MCP `agent-desktop mcp` serves every command as an MCP tool over stdio. A tool is named after its command (`desktop_snapshot`, `desktop_click`, `desktop_session_start`), takes that command's arguments, and returns its JSON envelope: ```json { "mcpServers": { "agent-desktop": { "command": "agent-desktop", "args": ["mcp"] } } } ``` Global flags given to `mcp`, such as `--session`, `--headed` or `--trace`, apply to every call. ## Commands agent-desktop has 60 command names, 56 operational commands. The other four (`key-down`, `key-up`, `mouse-down`, `mouse-up`) refuse to run until a daemon can release a held key or button. [Commands](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/commands) documents each one. | Group | Commands | |---|---| | Observe | `snapshot`, `find`, `get`, `is`, `screenshot`, `list-surfaces` | | Act on a ref | `click`, `double-click`, `triple-click`, `right-click`, `type`, `set-value`, `clear`, `focus`, `select`, `toggle`, `check`, `uncheck`, `expand`, `collapse`, `scroll`, `scroll-to` | | Keyboard and mouse | `press`, `hover`, `drag`, `mouse-move`, `mouse-click`, `mouse-wheel`, `key-down`, `key-up`, `mouse-down`, `mouse-up` | | Apps and windows | `launch`, `close-app`, `list-apps`, `list-windows`, `list-displays`, `focus-window`, `resize-window`, `move-window`, `minimize`, `maximize`, `restore`, `open-system-surface` | | Notifications | `list-notifications`, `dismiss-notification`, `dismiss-all-notifications`, `notification-action` | | Clipboard | `clipboard-get`, `clipboard-set`, `clipboard-clear` | | Wait | `wait` | | Sessions | `session`, `trace`, `cursor-overlay` | | System | `status`, `permissions`, `version`, `batch`, `skills` | ## Platform support | Platform | Requirement | Accessibility API | |---|---|---| | [macOS](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/platforms/macos) | macOS 13 or later, Intel or Apple Silicon | AX API | | [Windows](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/platforms/windows) | Windows 10 1809 or later, x64 or ARM64 | UI Automation | | [Linux](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/platforms/linux) | Ubuntu 24.04 or later, x86_64 or aarch64, X11 or Wayland | AT-SPI | Each platform page lists what works headless, what needs `--headed`, and what refuses. ## C library Each release ships `libagent_desktop_ffi`, so a program can call agent-desktop in process. See the [C library docs](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/ffi). ```python import ctypes lib = ctypes.CDLL("./lib/libagent_desktop_ffi.dylib") lib.ad_adapter_create.restype = ctypes.c_void_p lib.ad_adapter_destroy.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p] assert lib.ad_init(7) == 0 # AD_RESULT_OK when the header's AD_ABI_VERSION_MAJOR matches the library adapter = lib.ad_adapter_create() lib.ad_adapter_destroy(adapter) ``` ## Development Each platform adapter builds only on its own OS, so scope cargo to the host's packages. On macOS: ```bash HOST_PKGS=(-p agent-desktop-core -p agent-desktop-macos -p agent-desktop -p agent-desktop-ffi) cargo test "${HOST_PKGS[@]}" cargo clippy "${HOST_PKGS[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings ``` On Windows, use `agent-desktop-windows` instead of `agent-desktop-macos`; on Linux, `agent-desktop-linux`. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) lists every gate. ## Documentation - [Introduction](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop): what it is and how it works - [Snapshots and refs](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/snapshots-and-refs) - [Errors and recovery](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/errors-and-recovery) - [Skills](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/skills) - [CONCEPTS.md](CONCEPTS.md): vocabulary - [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md) ## License Apache-2.0

[workspace]
members         = ["crates/core", "crates/macos", "crates/windows", "crates/linux", "crates/ffi", "src"]
default-members = ["crates/core", "crates/macos", "crates/windows", "crates/linux", "src"]
resolver = "2"

[workspace.package]
edition      = "2024"
rust-version = "1.89"
license      = "Apache-2.0"
version      = "1.2.0"

[workspace.dependencies]
clap               = { version = "4.6", features = ["derive"] }
serde              = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json         = { version = "1.0", features = ["float_roundtrip"] }
thiserror          = "2.0"
tracing            = "0.1"
tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3", features = ["env-filter"] }
base64             = "0.23"
rustc-hash         = "2.1"
libc               = "0.2"
smallvec           = { version = "1.13", features = ["serde", "union"] }
agent-desktop-core = { path = "crates/core" }

[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn = "warn"
unreachable_pub        = "allow"
unused_must_use        = "deny"
let_underscore_drop    = "allow"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
dbg_macro              = "deny"
todo                   = "warn"
needless_collect       = "warn"
redundant_clone        = "allow"
unwrap_used            = "allow"
expect_used            = "allow"
needless_pass_by_value = "allow"
manual_let_else        = "allow"
items_after_statements = "allow"
collapsible_if         = "allow"
print_stdout           = "allow"
print_stderr           = "allow"

[profile.release]
opt-level     = "z"
lto           = true
codegen-units = 1
strip         = true
panic         = "abort"

[profile.release.package.agent-desktop-core]
opt-level = 3

[profile.release.package.agent-desktop-macos]
opt-level = 3

[profile.ci]
inherits      = "release"
opt-level     = 1
lto           = false
codegen-units = 16
strip         = false
debug         = 1

[profile.release-ffi]
inherits = "release"
panic    = "unwind"

description: The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder, review with critique and audit, catch AI slop before it ships.
readme_content:
# Impeccable The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with `polish` and `bolder`, review with `critique` and `audit`, and catch AI slop before it ships. From your project root: ```bash npx impeccable install ``` Reload your coding tool, then run `/impeccable init` in your agent (`$impeccable init` on Codex). Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). | Without Impeccable | With Impeccable | |---|---| | ![Villa Castagneto built without Impeccable: cream background, a thin serif headline with an italic accent, two pill buttons, and flat vector illustrations in rounded cards](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-without.webp) | ![Villa Castagneto built with Impeccable: a full-bleed engraved night scene of the villa on its cliff above the sea, a condensed cream and vermilion headline, and a month strip along the bottom](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-with.webp) | Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water. For a full project, see the [Neo Mirai case study](https://impeccable.style/cases/neo-mirai): a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page. ## Why Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects. - **Words for what you want.** "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. `/impeccable bolder the pricing cards` loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target. - **A reviewer.** `critique` scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. `audit` checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish). - **A slop detector.** 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key. Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see [Build something new](https://impeccable.style/docs/new-work) for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component: ``` /impeccable critique the pricing cards ``` ## How it works Run `/impeccable init` once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes `PRODUCT.md`. Every later command reads it. Run `/impeccable document` to capture your existing visual system in `DESIGN.md`, so changes stay on-brand. [More on context files](https://impeccable.style/docs/context). Then name a command and a target: ``` /impeccable critique the onboarding flow /impeccable quieter the landing page /impeccable polish settings /impeccable harden checkout ``` Or just describe what you want: `/impeccable redo this hero section`. Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with `/impeccable pin audit` to get `/audit` as its own shortcut. ### 24 commands | | Commands | |---|---| | **Steer** | `bolder` amplifies safe designs · `quieter` tones down loud ones · `distill` removes what the page doesn't need · `colorize` brings color to a gray interface · `typeset` fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · `layout` fixes spacing and rhythm · `animate` adds transitions and interaction feedback · `delight` adds personality · `overdrive` goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects | | **Review** | `critique` is a scored UX review · `audit` is a technical quality report | | **Finish** | `polish` is the final pass before shipping · `harden` covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · `clarify` rewrites unclear copy · `adapt` handles screen sizes and devices · `optimize` fixes loading and rendering performance · `onboard` designs first-run flows and empty states | | **Iterate live** | `live` lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · `generate` produces variants of a named element without manual picking | | **Plan and set up** | `shape` plans UX before code · `init` writes `PRODUCT.md` · `document` writes `DESIGN.md` · `extract` pulls repeated patterns into your design system | The 24th, `craft`, is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type `/impeccable` alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). On Codex, open `/skills` or type `$impeccable` instead of the slash command. ### Live mode `/impeccable live` opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. [Iterate in the browser](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/iterate-live). Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your `package.json`'s optional `impeccable:manual-edit-validate` script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo. Apply sends staged copy edits to your chat agent while a live session is polling. If none has polled in the last minute, it runs the `codex` CLI from your PATH instead (or `claude` when codex is missing), with approvals, permission checks, and sandboxing off (`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` or `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`) and your environment inherited. Its prompt carries the staged edits, the edited elements' HTML and nearby text, the page URL, and candidate source paths. Set `IMPECCABLE_LIVE_COPY_AGENT=chat` in the environment that starts live mode to keep Apply in your chat session, or `off` to disable Apply. The server reads it once at startup. ## Three ways to run the detector **In your agent.** The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. [Automatic design checks](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks). **In CI or your terminal.** The CLI needs no agent: ```bash npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge) npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description ``` Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: `npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173`. Exit code `2` means findings, `1` means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run `npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font"`. To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: ``. [Run a detector scan](https://impeccable.style/docs/detector) · [Configuration and ignores](https://impeccable.style/docs/config). **In your browser.** The [Chrome extension](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/impeccable/bdkgmiklpdmaojlpflclinlofgjfpabf) overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. [Review with a visual overlay](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/critique-with-overlay). ## Installation ```bash npx impeccable install ``` The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. `npx impeccable update` refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass `--providers=claude,codex,cursor` and `--scope=project|global`. Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open `/hooks` and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run `/hooks-trust` or launch with `--trust`. In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run `hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook` once. [Allow the hook in your harness](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks#allow-the-hook-in-your-harness). Node is only needed for `npx`. The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into `~/.impeccable/bin/`.
Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins **Claude Code:** `/plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable`, then open `/plugin` and install Impeccable. **GitHub Copilot in VS Code:** install [Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=renaissance-geek.impeccable) or run `code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable`. Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. [Details](docs/VSCODE-EXTENSION.md). **Grok Build:** `grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust` installs the skill, agents, and hook.
Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team) ```bash git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor ``` Commit `.gitmodules`, the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run `git submodule update --init --recursive`. To upgrade, run `git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable`, rerun the `link` command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass `--force`.
Manual copy, no Node required Download the ZIP for your tool from [impeccable.style](https://impeccable.style), or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy `skills/impeccable` from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder. | Tool | Repo folder | Global skills folder | |---|---|---| | Claude Code | `.claude/` | `~/.claude/skills/` | | Cursor | `.cursor/` | | | Codex CLI, Replit Agent | `.agents/` | `~/.agents/skills/` | | Devin | `.devin/` | `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/` | | GitHub Copilot | `.github/` | | | Gemini CLI | `.gemini/` | | | Google Antigravity | `.agent/` | `~/.gemini/config/skills/` | | OpenCode | `.opencode/` | | | Grok Build | `.grok/` | `~/.grok/skills/` | | Hermes Agent | `.hermes/` | `${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/` | | DeepSeek Harness | `.dsh/` | `${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/` | | Pi | `.pi/` | | | Qoder | `.qoder/` | `~/.qoder/skills/` | | Rovo Dev | `.rovodev/` | `~/.rovodev/skills/` | | Mistral Vibe | `.vibe/` | `~/.vibe/skills/` | | Trae | `.trae/` | `~/.trae/skills/` | | Trae China | `.trae-cn/` | `~/.trae-cn/skills/` | For example: `mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/`. name: claude-mem
description: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent – Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More

🇨🇳 中文 • 🇹🇼 繁體中文 • 🇯🇵 日本語 • 🇵🇹 Português • 🇧🇷 Português • 🇰🇷 한국어 • 🇪🇸 Español • 🇩🇪 Deutsch • 🇫🇷 Français • 🇮🇱 עברית • 🇸🇦 العربية • 🇷🇺 Русский • 🇵🇱 Polski • 🇨🇿 Čeština • 🇳🇱 Nederlands • 🇹🇷 Türkçe • 🇺🇦 Українська • 🇻🇳 Tiếng Việt • 🇵🇭 Tagalog • 🇮🇩 Indonesia • 🇹🇭 ไทย • 🇮🇳 हिन्दी • 🇧🇩 বাংলা • 🇵🇰 اردو • 🇷🇴 Română • 🇸🇪 Svenska • 🇮🇹 Italiano • 🇬🇷 Ελληνικά • 🇭🇺 Magyar • 🇫🇮 Suomi • 🇩🇰 Dansk • 🇳🇴 Norsk

Your coding agent forgets everything between sessions. Claude-Mem remembers for it.


Quick Start • How It Works • Search Tools • Documentation • Configuration • Troubleshooting • License

Every new session, your agent starts from zero. It re-reads the same files, re-asks the same questions, and walks back into mistakes you already fixed together.

Claude-Mem runs a second agent beside it that takes notes while it works. The next session starts with a short index of what matters, and pulls in the details only when it needs them. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and 11 more agents. Copilot CLI, Goose, Roo Code and Warp can search your memory, but their sessions aren't recorded.

--- ## Quick Start **Installing for someone as an AI agent?** Run `npx claude-mem install --runtime worker` on their computer in an interactive terminal (enable PTY in your shell tool). It first asks in the terminal which agents to set up and, for Claude Code, whether to disable native auto-memory (and whether to overwrite an existing install). Relay each question to the user and type their answer, or pass `--ide ` to skip the first one. Keep the installer running. When it prints **Continue setup in your browser**, open that URL in the user's browser if the installer hasn't already opened it. Let the user go through setup and make their own choices, including the usage-analytics question the installer may ask at the end. If you can't run an interactive terminal on their computer, give them the command to run locally. ```bash npx claude-mem install ``` The installer finds the agents on your machine and asks which ones to set up. Then just start working: observations stream in from your first prompt, and your second session in a project opens with memory from the first. (Copilot CLI, Goose, Roo Code and Warp get memory search only, so their sessions don't add to it.) The installer sets everything up first, then asks you to sign in to claude-mem in your browser (email magic link, no card required to sign in). Choosing the **claude-mem observer** then starts its **30 Day Free Trial** on a checkout page that asks for a payment method; once it completes, the installer saves your memory key. With the observer, memory runs off-plan, so you get up to 100% more usage from your plan. When the free trial ends, memory automatically falls back to your Anthropic plan unless you subscribe. After sign-in you pick your memory provider: the claude-mem observer, your own OpenRouter or Gemini key, or your Anthropic plan. Prefer to skip the sign-in? Pass an explicit `--provider` flag, set `CLAUDE_MEM_ONLINE_OPTIN=false`, or run in CI/non-interactive shells — the installer completes without any account interaction. Your memory lives in `~/.claude-mem` on your machine. Cloud sync is opt-in. Anonymous usage analytics are on by default; `npx claude-mem telemetry disable` turns them off ([what's collected](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/telemetry)). Or install from the plugin marketplace inside Claude Code: ```bash /plugin marketplace add thedotmack/claude-mem /plugin install claude-mem ``` Restart Claude Code. Context from previous sessions will automatically appear in new sessions. > **Note:** Claude-Mem is also published on npm, but `npm install -g claude-mem` installs the **SDK/library only** — it does not register the plugin hooks or set up the worker service. Always install via `npx claude-mem install` or the `/plugin` commands above. ### Other agents `npx claude-mem install` covers every supported agent. To set up one agent directly, pass `--ide`. **OpenCode** (1.3.4 or later, including OpenCode 2). Restart OpenCode after installing. ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide opencode ``` **T3 Code** (Codex and Claude Code providers). The installer discovers T3 Code's enabled providers, registers native Claude-Mem plugins in their configured homes, and supports T3-managed Codex. Restart T3 Code, trust the provider's hooks when prompted, and start a new thread. See the [T3 Code integration guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/t3code-integration) for custom server settings, status, and removal. ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide t3code ``` **Antigravity CLI** ([setup guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/antigravity-cli/setup)): ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide antigravity ``` **OMP (Oh My Pi):** ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide omp ``` **Pi and DeepSeek Harness** use the worker runtime. See [native harness setup](docs/native-harness-integrations.md) for capture, recall, and troubleshooting. ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide pi npx claude-mem install --ide dsh --dsh-profile tui ``` **Grok Bot:** see [Grok Bot](#grok-bot) below. ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide grok-bot ``` The full list of `--ide` values is in `npx claude-mem --help`. #### Grok Bot Grok Bot has no host hooks, so we watch the chat log files. Default is CMEM Pro, the hosted memory. Local observer is opt-in: `--provider host`. Installing this plugin does not install Cursor. **Opt-in awareness push:** needle observations (`decision`, `bugfix`, `security_alert`, `sensitive`) are appended as dated `- YYYY-MM-DD [awareness] …` lines into that bot's `memory/log/YYYY-MM.md`. Grok Bot already re-reads the log from disk. This does not write `profile.md`, user-memory, or project memory. Enable with `CLAUDE_MEM_GROK_BOT_AWARENESS_ENABLED=true` and set `CLAUDE_MEM_GROK_BOT_AWARENESS_AGENT_IDS` to your agent UUIDs (empty by default). #### 🦞 OpenClaw Gateway Install claude-mem as a persistent memory plugin on [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai) gateways with a single command: ```bash curl -fsSL https://install.cmem.ai/openclaw.sh | bash ``` The installer handles dependencies, plugin setup, AI provider configuration, worker startup, and optional real-time observation feeds to Telegram, Discord, Slack, and more. See the [OpenClaw Integration Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/openclaw-integration) for details. ## What You Get - 🧠 **The next session starts where the last one left off.** Each session opens with a compact index of past observations, layered so the agent opens full details only when it needs them, and the header can show what each layer costs in tokens. - 🔍 **Find anything you worked on.** The mem-search skill searches your project history in three steps (index, timeline, details), so the agent spends tokens only on what it opens. - 🖥️ **Watch it work, and keep track of yours.** My Work shows live requests, progress, human handoffs and a saved review queue at the worker URL printed on startup. --- https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/043ec09f-4bdd-41d5-aee0-8fda6b83e267 **the runtime your coding agents live on.** - **detach without stopping work** — herdr keeps terminals running in a background server when you close the client or lose your SSH connection. after a server or machine restart, herdr restores the saved layout and can resume supported agent sessions; the original processes do not survive. [session state →](https://herdr.dev/docs/session-state/) - **several machines, one window** — keep local work and saved ssh machines together, with a combined agent list and independent reconnects. [remote machines →](https://herdr.dev/docs/connecting-machines/) - **never hunt for the stuck one** — every pane is marked working, blocked, or idle. when an agent stops and needs an answer, herdr says so. - **agent-native** — agents drive herdr through the cli and socket api: they can spawn panes, prompt each other, and wait until another agent is genuinely blocked. [agent skill →](https://herdr.dev/docs/agent-skill/) - **runs what you already run** — claude code, codex, cursor, opencode, grok and the rest. herdr doesn't wrap or replace them; it owns their terminals. building an agent? [add herdr support →](https://herdr.dev/docs/add-herdr-support/) - **keyboard and mouse, both first-class** — tmux-style prefix keys *and* click, drag, split. pick per moment, not per tool. - **plugins** — extend panes and workflows. [browse the marketplace →](https://herdr.dev/plugins/) - **one rust binary, no electron** — runs in whatever terminal you already use. --- ## install ```bash curl -fsSL https://herdr.dev/install.sh | sh ``` or `brew install herdr` · `mise use -g herdr` · windows: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm https://herdr.dev/install.ps1 | iex"` · [endpoint-protected Windows](https://herdr.dev/docs/windows-beta/) · [binaries](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/releases) then start it where the work lives: ```bash herdr ``` run your agents, split panes, walk away. `ctrl+b q` detaches, `herdr` reattaches. [quick start →](https://herdr.dev/docs/quick-start/) ## docs everything lives at [herdr.dev/docs](https://herdr.dev/docs/): [quick start](https://herdr.dev/docs/quick-start/) · [concepts](https://herdr.dev/docs/concepts/) · [supported agents](https://herdr.dev/docs/agents/) · [keyboard](https://herdr.dev/docs/keyboard/) · [configuration](https://herdr.dev/docs/configuration/) · [session state](https://herdr.dev/docs/session-state/) · [connecting machines](https://herdr.dev/docs/connecting-machines/) · [remote](https://herdr.dev/docs/persistence-remote/) · [integrations](https://herdr.dev/docs/integrations/) · [add herdr support to your agent](https://herdr.dev/docs/add-herdr-support/) · [plugins](https://herdr.dev/docs/plugins/) · [socket api](https://herdr.dev/docs/socket-api/) ## thanks every past sponsor and backer is listed in [SPONSORS.md](./SPONSORS.md) — thank you 🐑 enterprise / partnership: hey@herdr.dev ## agent instructions if you are an ai agent helping with this repository, read [`AGENTS.md`](./AGENTS.md) before making changes and read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening issues or PRs. ## development ```bash git clone https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr cd herdr cargo build --release just test # unit tests just check # formatting, tests, and maintenance checks ``` ## license Herdr is licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE).

description: ⌥ Coding agent with the IDE wired in. Built by Stencil Labs.
readme_content:
A coding agent with the IDE wired in. omp.sh

Language: English | 简体中文

Built by Stencil Labs · Fork of Pi by @mariozechner

The most capable agent surface that ships. Continuously tuned by real-world use — complete out of the box, open all the way down. **60+** providers · **31** built-in tools · **14** lsp ops · **28** dap ops · **~80k** lines of Rust core. > [!NOTE] > Pull requests are **temporarily open to everyone** as a trial. We previously > required a vouch before accepting PRs; that requirement is lifted for now > while we evaluate how open contributions go. Depending on the results, the > vouch system may return. ## Install **macOS · Linux** ```sh curl -fsSL https://omp.sh/install | sh ``` Without a usable bun (or with `--binary`), the install scripts fetch the prebuilt binary from `build.stencil.so` and check its SHA-256 before installing it. Pin a release with `curl -fsSL https://omp.sh/install | sh -s -- --binary --ref v` (PowerShell: `-Binary -Ref v`). > **Alpine / musl:** the prebuilt musl binary links `libstdc++`/`libgcc` dynamically, which stock Alpine does not ship. Install them first: `apk add libstdc++ libgcc`. **Homebrew** ```sh brew install can1357/tap/omp ``` **Bun (recommended)** ```sh bun install -g @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent ``` **Nix** ```sh # Run without installing nix run github:can1357/oh-my-pi # Or install into the active profile (Nix < 2.30: `nix profile install`) nix profile add github:can1357/oh-my-pi ``` Flake consumers can use `packages..omp`, `overlays.default`, `nixosModules.default`, or `homeManagerModules.default`. A Home Manager configuration can install OMP and own its settings declaratively: ```nix { inputs.omp.url = "github:can1357/oh-my-pi"; # In your Home Manager module: imports = [ inputs.omp.homeManagerModules.default ]; programs.omp = { enable = true; settings.startup.quiet = true; }; } ``` **Windows (PowerShell)** ```powershell irm https://omp.sh/install.ps1 | iex ``` **Pinned versions (mise)** ```sh mise use -g github:can1357/oh-my-pi ``` macOS · Linux · Windows · bun ≥ 1.4.4 ### Shell completions `omp` generates its own completion scripts for **bash**, **zsh**, and **fish** from the live command/flag metadata, so they never drift from the actual CLI. Subcommands, flags, and enum values complete statically; model names (`--model`, `--smol`, `--slow`, `--plan`) resolve against the bundled model catalog and `--resume` against your on-disk sessions. ```sh # zsh — add to ~/.zshrc (or write the output into a file on your $fpath) eval "$(omp completions zsh)" # bash — add to ~/.bashrc eval "$(omp completions bash)" # fish omp completions fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/omp.fish ``` ## Every tool, _benchmaxxed_. Edits that land on the first attempt. Reads that summarize files instead of dumping their content. Searches that return instantly. Pick any model — omp will get it right. | model | metric | what | | ---------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Grok Code Fast 1 | 6.7% → 68.3% | Tenfold lift the moment the edit format stops eating the model alive. | | Gemini 3 Flash | +5 pp | Over str_replace — beats Google's own best attempt at the format. | | Grok 4 Fast | −61% tokens | Output collapses once the retry loop on bad diffs disappears. | | MiniMax | 2.1× | Pass rate more than doubles. Same weights, same prompt. | - `read` : summarized snippets · ideal defaults · selector hit rate - `grep` : fastest in the west - `lsp` : everything your IDE knows, the agent knows - `prompts` : adjusted relentlessly for each model [Read the full post ↗](https://blog.can.ac/2026/02/12/the-harness-problem/) ## The Pi _you love_, with **batteries included**. Originally built on [Mario Zechner](https://github.com/mariozechner)'s wonderful [Pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono), omp adds everything you're missing. ### 01 · Code execution w/ tool-calling Most harnesses give the agent a Python sandbox and call it done. Ours runs persistent Python and a Bun worker, and either kernel can call back into the agent's own tools — read, search, task — over a loopback bridge. The agent loads a CSV with tool.read from inside Python, charts it from JavaScript, and never leaves the cell. ![omp TUI running Python code and rendering a chart.](assets/python.webp) ### 02 · LSP wired into every write Ask for a rename and you get a rename. The call goes through workspace/willRenameFiles, so re-exports, barrel files, and aliased imports update before the file moves. Everything your IDE knows, the agent knows. ![omp TUI with TypeScript and Biome language servers active.](assets/lspv.webp) _[Read the LSP config docs](docs/lsp-config.md)_ ### 03 · Drives a real debugger A C binary segfaults: the agent attaches lldb, steps to the bad pointer, reads the frame. A Go service hangs: it attaches dlv and walks the goroutines. A Python process is wedged: debugpy, pause, inspect, evaluate. Most agents are still sprinkling print statements. ![omp TUI: a live lldb-dap session against a native binary at /tmp/omp-native/demo. Adapter=lldb-dap, Status=stopped, Frame=xorshift32, Instruction pointer 0x10000055C, Location demo.c:6:10. Debug scopes and Debug variables cards show locals (x = 57351) and the agent confirms the math: x went from 7 → 57351 (= 7 ^ (7<<13)).](https://omp.sh/clips/dap-poster.webp) _[Watch the capture ↗](https://omp.sh/clips/dap.mp4)_ ### 04 · Time-traveling stream rules Your rules sit dormant until the model goes off-script. A regex match aborts the stream mid-token, injects the rule as a system reminder, and retries from the same point. You get course-correction without paying context tax on every turn. Injections survive compaction, so the fix sticks. ![omp TUI: agent reading src.rs and about to write Box::leak when the request aborts (red `Error: Request was aborted`), an amber `⚠ Injecting rule: box-leak` card injects the rule body `Don't reach for Box::leak in production code paths`, and the agent then course-corrects by proposing `Arc` and asking the user to confirm.](https://omp.sh/clips/ttsr-poster.webp) _[Watch the capture ↗](https://omp.sh/clips/ttsr.mp4)_ ### 05 · First-class subagents Split a job across workers and get typed results back. task fans out into isolated worktrees, each worker runs its own tool surface, and the final yield is a schema-validated object the parent reads directly. No prose to parse, no merge conflicts between siblings, no orphaned edits. ![omp TUI showing `task` spawning two subagents `ComponentsExports` and `RoutesExports`, the constraints block requiring an IRC DM between peers, the per-subagent status cards with cost and duration, and a final Findings section listing both exports plus an honest 'IRC coordination note' about a one-sided handshake.](https://omp.sh/clips/irc-poster.webp) _[Watch the capture ↗](https://omp.sh/clips/irc.mp4)_ Watch the fan-out while it runs: `Alt+A` opens [Agent Hub](docs/agent-hub.md), where the roster shows current activity and usage for every subagent. Open one to read its live transcript, type a steering message, revive a parked worker, or kill a stuck one without aborting the parent session. ### 06 · A second model, watching every turn. Pair a reviewer model to the 'advisor' role and it reads every turn the main agent takes, injecting notes inline — a quiet aside, a concern, or a hard blocker. It runs on its own context and its own model, so it catches what the doer rushed past. The main agent sees the note and course-corrects, or tells you why it won't. ![omp TUI: /advisor status shows the advisor running on openai-codex/gpt-5.5; after the main agent scopes a catch to ENOENT instead of swallowing every error, an amber 'Advisor 1 note (concern)' card warns the fix no longer matches the user's literal acceptance criterion.](https://omp.sh/clips/advisor-poster.webp) _[Watch the capture ↗](https://omp.sh/clips/advisor.mp4)_ ### 07 · Hand someone the link, they're in. /collab puts your live session on a relay and hands back a link — and a QR. A teammate joins from another terminal with omp join, or just opens it in a browser. Share read-write to pair on the same agent, or /collab view for a read-only link anyone can watch but no one can steer. Frames are sealed client-side; the relay never sees your keys. ![omp TUI: /collab view prints 'Collab session started!' with an omp join command, a my.omp.sh browser link, the note 'Anyone with this link can watch the session but cannot prompt the agent', and a large scannable QR code.](https://omp.sh/clips/collab-poster.webp) _[Watch the capture ↗](https://omp.sh/clips/collab.mp4)_ ### 08 · Read a pdf on arxiv, why not? web_search chains twenty-four ranked providers and hands whatever URLs it finds straight to read. Arxiv PDFs, GitHub pages, Stack Overflow threads come back as structured markdown with anchors intact — the same tool surface you use on local files. Cite, follow, quote, never lose where you came from. ![omp TUI: web_search returns 10 ranked Perplexity sources for inference-time compute scaling, the agent picks an arxiv paper, calls read https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.10739v1, and summarizes the paper's headline result with real numbers.](https://omp.sh/clips/web-poster.webp) _[Watch the capture ↗](https://omp.sh/clips/web.mp4)_ ### 09 · Unapologetically native. Even on Windows. Other agents shell out to rg, grep, find, and bash. On many machines those binaries don't exist, and on the ones where they do, every call costs a fork-exec round-trip. omp links the real implementations into the process. ripgrep, glob, find: in-process. The bash is our own bash 5.3 engine — with sessions that survive across calls, and 58 command-line utilities (ls, sed, sort, xargs, even jq) ported into the builtins crate and run in-process, zero fork/exec. The same omp binary runs on macOS, Linux, and Wi

readme_content:
Cloud | Documentation | Roadmap | Discord

📕 Table of Contents - 💡 [What is RAGFlow?](#-what-is-ragflow) - 🎮 [Get Started](#-get-started) - 🔥 [Latest Updates](#-latest-updates) - 🌟 [Key Features](#-key-features) - 🔎 [System Architecture](#-system-architecture) - 🏠 [Local Deployment](#-local-deployment) - 📚 [Documentation](#-documentation) - 📜 [Roadmap](#-roadmap) - 🏄 [Community](#-community) - 🙌 [Contributing](#-contributing)
## 💡 What is RAGFlow? [RAGFlow](https://ragflow.io/) is a leading open-source Retrieval-Augmented Generation ([RAG](https://ragflow.io/basics/what-is-rag)) engine that fuses cutting-edge RAG with Agent capabilities to create a superior context layer for LLMs. It offers a streamlined RAG workflow adaptable to enterprises of any scale. Powered by a converged [context engine](https://ragflow.io/basics/what-is-agent-context-engine) and pre-built agent templates, RAGFlow enables developers to transform complex data into high-fidelity, production-ready AI systems with exceptional efficiency and precision. ## 🎮 Get Started Try our cloud service at [https://cloud.ragflow.io](https://cloud.ragflow.io). For local deployment, see [Local Deployment](#-local-deployment).
## 🔥 Latest Updates - 2026-09-29 RAGFlow 1.0.0-rc1 released. - 2026-09-10 Added website content ingestion through sitemaps. - 2026-08-19 Introduced Knowledge Compilation to generate Wikis, Graphs, Trees, PageIndex, Mind Maps, Timelines, and Skills at the document and dataset levels. - 2026-08-19 Introduced Agentic RAG with Low, Medium, High, and Ultra thinking modes. - 2026-07-02 Added Google BigQuery data source ingestion and incremental synchronization. See the [full release notes](https://ragflow.io/docs/dev/release_notes) for more updates. ## 🌟 Key Features ### 🍭 **"Quality in, quality out"** - Deep document understanding-based knowledge extraction from unstructured data with complicated formats. - Finds "needle in a data haystack" of literally unlimited tokens. ### 🍱 **Template-based chunking** - Intelligent and explainable. - Plenty of template options to choose from. ### 🧩 **Knowledge Compilation** - Compile content at the document and dataset levels into structured knowledge artifacts. - Use compilation templates to generate Wikis, Graphs, Trees, PageIndex, Mind Maps, Timelines, and Skills for different knowledge organization and reuse needs. - Configure compilation models and processing rules, and view, update, and regenerate knowledge artifacts. ### 🧠 **Agentic Retrieval** - Perform multi-step retrieval for complex questions: the model analyzes the question and, when needed, breaks it down, retrieves knowledge, and verifies evidence. - Gather more complete context through multiple rounds of retrieval and reasoning to help generate well-grounded answers. - Choose Low, Medium, High, or Ultra thinking modes to control retrieval and reasoning depth according to question complexity. ### 🌱 **Grounded citations with reduced hallucinations** - Visualization of text chunking to allow human intervention. - Quick view of the key references and traceable citations to support grounded answers. ### 🍔 **Compatibility with heterogeneous data sources** - Supports Word documents, PowerPoint presentations, Excel spreadsheets, TXT files, images, PDFs, scanned copies, structured data, web pages, and more. ### 🛀 **Automated and effortless RAG workflow** - Streamlined RAG orchestration catered to both personal and large businesses. - Configurable LLMs as well as embedding models. - Multiple recall paired with fused re-ranking. - Intuitive APIs for seamless integration with business. ## 🔎 System Architecture
## 🏠 Local Deployment Local deployment supports both Docker deployment and launching from source. Docker is suitable for quick evaluation, integration testing, and production deployment, while launching from source is intended for RAGFlow development and debugging. Docker deployment does not require a Go compiler. Launching from source requires the Go version specified in `go.mod`; frontend development additionally requires Node.js and npm. ### 🐳 Docker Deployment #### 📝 Docker Deployment Prerequisites - Recommended starting configuration: 4 CPU cores, 16 GB RAM, and 50 GB of available disk space. Actual requirements depend on the document engine, data volume, parsing tasks, and concurrency. Local models and other optional components may require additional resources. - Docker ≥ 24.0.0, Docker Compose ≥ v2.26.1. > [!TIP] > If you have not installed Docker on your local machine (Windows, macOS, or Linux), see [Install Docker Engine](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/). #### 🚀 Start up the server 1. If using Elasticsearch, set `vm.max_map_count` on the Docker host to at least 262144. This step is usually unnecessary with Infinity: > To check the value of `vm.max_map_count`: > > ```bash > sysctl vm.max_map_count > ``` > > If you use Elasticsearch and the value is below 262144, reset it: > > ```bash > # In this case, we set it to 262144: > sudo sysctl -w vm.max_map_count=262144 > ``` > > This change will be reset after a system reboot. To ensure your change remains permanent, add or update the `vm.max_map_count` value in **/etc/sysctl.conf** accordingly: > > ```bash > vm.max_map_count=262144 > ``` 2. Clone the repository: ```bash git clone https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow.git ``` 3. Check out the release tag and start the server with Docker Compose: Enter the Docker deployment directory. ```bash cd ragflow/docker ``` Check out the `v1.0.0` release tag. ```bash git checkout v1.0.0 ``` Start the RAGFlow services and their dependencies. ```bash docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up -d ``` With the default MySQL configuration, the image entrypoint runs database migrations before starting Admin, Syncer, Ingestor, API, and other services. > In the RAGFlow open-source 1.0 release, DeepDoc uses CPU inference for layout analysis, OCR, and table recognition. 4. Check the server status after startup: Use `docker ps` to check the dependency services. After the dependencies show `healthy` and the RAGFlow container remains running, use the HTTP endpoint to determine whether RAGFlow is ready. The RAGFlow container itself does not define a Compose healthcheck. ```bash curl -f http://localhost/api/v1/system/healthz ``` After receiving an HTTP 200 response, open the Web UI. If you changed `SVR_WEB_HTTP_PORT`, replace the port in the health-check URL accordingly. If startup fails, inspect the container logs: ```bash docker logs --tail 50 ragflow-cpu ``` 5. In your web browser, enter the IP address of your server and log in to RAGFlow. > With the default settings, you only need to enter `http://IP_OF_YOUR_MACHINE` (**without** port number), because the default HTTP serving port `80` can be omitted when using the default configuration. 6. After signing in, add an LLM, embedding, and reranker on the model provider page, including the model name, service address, and API key. > For details, see [llm_api_key_setup](https://ragflow.io/docs/dev/llm_api_key_setup). _The show is on!_ See the [Quickstart guide](./docs/quickstart.mdx) for details. #### ⚙️ Docker Configuration and Adjustment Docker deployment uses `docker/.env` and `docker/docker-compose.yml`. Configure the image, ports, passwords, document engine, and model image source as described in the [Docker configuration guide](./docker/README.md). For platform support (note that macOS is not currently supported), see the [Go Docker image build and platform support guide](./docs/develop/build_docker_image.mdx). To build the Docker image from source, see the [Go Docker image build and platform support guide](./docs/develop/build_docker_image.mdx). For document-engine changes, configuration updates, restarting services, and retaining or removing existing data, follow the Docker configuration guide. ### 🔨 Launch from Source

readme_content:
Effortless Web Scraping for the Modern Web





Selection methods · Fetchers · Spiders · Proxy Rotation · CLI · MCP

Scrapling is a Python Web Scraping framework that brings fast HTTP requests, stealth browsers, powerful parsing, and concurrent crawling into one library. Scrape static pages, render JavaScript, interact with websites, and extract data from the API calls behind them. Build crawlers with reusable sessions, proxy rotation, automatic retries, pause/resume, and built-in data exports. Use it from Python, the terminal, or your AI agent through its MCP server and Agent Skill. From extracting a few fields to collecting a whole website as clean Markdown, Scrapling covers the full scraping workflow. ## What you can do with Scrapling - **[Fetch & interact](https://scrapling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/fetching/choosing.html)**: Fast HTTP requests, stealth browsers, JavaScript rendering, Cloudflare Turnstile/Interstitial handling, persistent sessions, and background API capture. - **[Parse & extract](https://scrapling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/parsing/selection.html)**: CSS, XPath, text and regex search, adaptive element tracking, similar-element matching, and clean Markdown output. - **[Crawl & export](https://scrapling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/spiders/getting-started.html)**: Concurrent spiders, proxy rotation, retries, AutoThrottle, pause/resume, streaming, ready-made templates, and JSON/JSONL/CSV/XML exports. - **[Scrape with AI or from your terminal](https://scrapling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ai/mcp-server.html)**: An MCP server for AI agents to browse and extract data, an Agent Skill, CLI commands, and an interactive shell. Start with a single page: ```python from scrapling.fetchers import Fetcher page = Fetcher.get('https://quotes.toscrape.com/') quotes = page.css('.quote .text::text').getall() print(quotes) ``` Or scale up with a spider: ```python from scrapling.spiders import Spider, Response class QuotesSpider(Spider): name = "quotes" start_urls = ["https://quotes.toscrape.com/"] async def parse(self, response: Response): for quote in response.css('.quote'): yield { "text": quote.css('.text::text').get(), "author": quote.css('.author::text').get(), } result = QuotesSpider().start() print(len(result.items)) result.items.to_json("quotes.json") ``` This prints `10` and saves the quotes and authors to `quotes.json`.
